beats.say: Conferences and official meetings are for making contacts. But someone there may also be collecting information.
A gifted flash drive, power bank or headset must not go into your work computer. It may carry malware.
Your badge shows your name, position and a QR code. Keep it out of photos and hide it outside.
Show every gifted device to technical support first. They will check it and decide.

scenes.title: After the forum
scenes.intro: You are back from the forum. There are gifts on your desk and new mail in your inbox.

steps.label: A gift from the visiting delegation
steps.say: The delegation gave you their presentation on a flash drive.

actions.label: Plug into computer
actions.feedback: You do not know what is on a gifted device. Technical support must check it first.

actions.label: Hand to technical support
actions.feedback: Correct. Technical support checks the device on a separate computer and passes the file on if needed.

steps.label: There is one file on the drive

actions.label: Open
actions.feedback: This is not a PDF but a shortcut. Opening it can run a hidden command.

actions.label: Eject device
actions.feedback: Right decision. Eject the device without opening the file and give it to technical support.

body.text: Dear colleague, I was very glad to meet you at the forum.
To plan our next meeting, could you send me a list of your department's staff with their positions and phone numbers?
Your manager's schedule for next week would also help.

steps.say: A guest you met at the forum writes to you.

actions.label: Send the list and schedule
actions.feedback: A staff list and a manager's schedule are a map for the next attack. Such data goes out only through official channels, with approval.

actions.label: Forward to manager and security
actions.feedback: Correct. The mail came from a personal address, and requests from outside parties go through official channels.

actions.label: Reply: Please send an official request
actions.feedback: Good. An official request is checked and answered by someone authorised.

body.text: "Forum Headset" wants to connect to this computer.

actions.label: Decline
actions.feedback: Correct. Never accept a pairing request you did not start yourself.

actions.label: Pair
actions.feedback: An unknown device can pose as a keyboard and type commands. Decline requests like this.

scenes.prompt: Find what this post should not reveal.

body.text: our delegation meets in the ministry's building 3.
I am at Lumera Hotel, room 512

spots.label: Badge
spots.explain: The badge shows name, position and an entry QR code. It can be used to forge a badge or to target you.

spots.label: Meeting time and place
spots.explain: A delegation's time and place are security information. Even after the meeting, keep it general.

spots.label: Hotel room
spots.explain: A room number shows who is staying where. Never share it anywhere.

question.prompt: The visiting delegation gives you a tablet as a gift. What do you do?

options.label: Tell my manager and give it to technical support to check
options.feedback: Correct. A gifted device is checked under your organisation's rules and joins the work network only with approval.

options.label: Set up my work mail on it right away
options.feedback: An unchecked device may carry spyware. Open work accounts only on your organisation's devices.

options.label: Take it home for personal use
options.feedback: The device could open a way into your home network and personal accounts too. Have it checked first.

options.label: Connect it to the office Wi-Fi to test it
options.feedback: Connecting an unchecked device to the work network opens a path to internal systems.

scenes.explain: Until it is checked, a gifted device is a stranger's device. Tell your manager and give it to technical support.

nodes.text: My presentation is on a flash drive. Shall we plug it into your computer?
nodes.speaker: Guest (at the meeting)
nodes.spoken: My presentation is on a flash drive. <breath> Shall we plug it into your computer?

choices.label: Let us open it on the separate computer technical support prepared
choices.feedback: Correct. The guest's files never touch the work computer or network.

choices.label: Go ahead, time is short
choices.feedback: An outside flash drive can bring malware onto a work computer. Use a separate computer for guests.

nodes.text: One more thing, what is the office Wi-Fi password? I need to check my mail.
nodes.speaker: Guest
nodes.spoken: One more thing, uh, what is the office Wi-Fi password? I need to check my mail.

choices.label: I give access to the guest network
choices.feedback: Correct. The guest network is kept apart from internal systems.

choices.label: I tell the work network password
choices.feedback: The work network carries internal systems. Guests get only the guest network.

nodes.text: Don't worry, I will look around the office myself.
nodes.speaker: Guest (during the break)
nodes.spoken: Don't worry, <breath> I will look around the office myself.

choices.label: I escort the guest
choices.feedback: Excellent. Guests always move around the office with an escort.

choices.label: Let them wander, they are our guest
choices.feedback: An unescorted guest can see open offices and documents on desks.

points: Hand gifted devices to technical support without plugging them in.
Do not share your badge, room number or schedule.
Guests get a separate computer, the guest network and an escort.
